prerequisites.title: X developer account
prerequisites.detail: Sign in at console.x.com with an X account, accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, and describe how you'll use the API.

prerequisites.title: API credits
prerequisites.detail: The API is pay-per-usage; credits are bought upfront in the Developer Console.

steps.title: Sign up for the developer account
steps.detail: Sign in at the Developer Console, accept the agreement and describe your use.

steps.title: Create app and enable OAuth 2.0
steps.detail: Create the app, enable OAuth 2.0 in authentication settings, and pick Web App or Automated App so you get a client secret.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are shown.

steps.title: Copy Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Take the callback URL from the Composio dashboard. Add it exactly to the app's Callback URLs.
steps.done_when: Callback URL saved in app settings.

steps.title: Save credentials immediately
steps.detail: Credentials are shown only once; regenerating invalidates the old ones.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret. Request only needed scopes plus offline.access.

steps.title: Buy API credits
steps.detail: Purchase credits in the Developer Console; costs vary by endpoint.

steps.title: Test a user connection
steps.detail: Connect a test account and confirm a refresh token is issued.
steps.done_when: Connected account stays valid beyond 2 hours.

steps.title: Contact your X representative
steps.detail: Apply for Standard Access for the extra Ads API endpoints you need.

traps.title: Access tokens expire after 2 hours
traps.detail: Without the offline.access scope no refresh token is issued, so users must reconnect.

traps.title: Credentials shown only once
traps.detail: If you lose them you must regenerate, which invalidates the old ones.

traps.title: Callback URL needs an exact match
traps.detail: The redirect URI must match one of the app's Callback URLs exactly.

traps.title: Costs can accrue within rate limits
traps.detail: Usage costs and rate limits are separate. Post reads are capped at 3 million per month on pay-per-usage.

traps.title: Full-archive search is restricted
traps.detail: It is only available with Academic Research access.

traps.title: Public client apps get no secret
traps.detail: Native and single-page app types are public clients; only confidential types get a client secret.

evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when available and suit building and iterating, with no OAuth app registration or credentials to manage.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio requests sensible defaults for each toolkit.
evidence.answer: Managed apps use Composio's default scopes, which are sensible defaults per toolkit; the default scopes may not include everything a developer needs.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: Managed apps show users a Composio consent screen during OAuth, not the developer's app name.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio." This is the most common reason to switch.
evidence.answer: In production, users should see the developer's app name rather than Composio; this is the most common reason to switch to a custom app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Composio's default scopes may not include everything needed, for example write access to a specific Google API.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share their rate-limit quota across all Composio users; a custom app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; a custom app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants of a toolkit (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Enterprise customers require your branding end-to-end.
evidence.answer: Enterprise customers who require the developer's branding end-to-end need a custom app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see [Managed OAuth apps](/toolkits/managed-auth).
evidence.answer: Whether Composio provides a managed OAuth app for a given toolkit is checked on the Managed OAuth apps page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest. Each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
evidence.answer: A developer can choose per toolkit: their own credentials for some toolkits and managed auth for others, with each toolkit getting its own auth config.

items.reason: The quote says to contact the X representative to apply for Standard Access in order to reach additional endpoints beyond app-level permissions.
The quote states the Authorization Code Flow with PKCE access token lasts two hours by default unless offline.access is used.
The quote says no refresh token is generated if the offline.access scope is not passed.
The quote says developers who requested Ads API access before July 2023 may have a limit of 5 user OAuth tokens.
The quote says to reach out to the X representative if the developer needs to increase the app's token limit.
The quote states X does not increase rate limits for any Ads API endpoint.
The quote states X API uses pay-per-usage pricing with no subscriptions, paying only for what is used.
The quote says to purchase credits upfront in the Developer Console and that they are deducted as requests are made.
The quote caps pay-per-usage plans at 3 million Post reads per monthly billing cycle and directs higher volume to an Enterprise plan.
The quote says one can be within rate limits but still incur usage costs, or hit rate limits without additional cost.
The quote says full-archive search is only available to those with Academic Research access.
The quote lists the scopes tweet.read, tweet.write and users.read, but does not itself tie them to posting and deleting Tweets.
The quote states an OAuth 2.0 refresh token is issued when the offline.access scope is applied.
The quote advises developers to request only the OAuth permissions their app needs.
The quote says the user cannot access Campaign Management, Creative or Custom Audiences endpoints and can only pull metrics through Analytics endpoints.

The quotes state the onboarding prerequisites: sign in to the console, accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, then create an app. The quotes do not name the specific agent setup, but the prerequisites are stated generally.
The quotes state pay-per-usage pricing with no subscriptions, credits purchased upfront, and credits deducted per API request.

The quote says to apply for Standard Access through an X representative, which is an application to the provider, but it does not explicitly say the provider reviews, verifies or approves the app before use, installation or listing.
The quote gives the steps in order: reach out to the X representative, then apply for Standard Access.
The quote supports the 5-token limit for apps requested before July 2023 and the route to increase it, but does not say the limit applies 'before approval'.
The quotes say to review and accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, and after signing up create an app to get API credentials.
The quote supports that Standard Access is applied for through an X representative, but nothing in the quotes gives the roughly one-hour build time, the review status, or the unknown wait time.
